evals.prompt: We're a 6-person agency and our knowledge is everywhere: 30+ PDFs (proposals, audits), a folder of sales call transcripts from tl;dv, two pitch decks, and a pricing spreadsheet. I want Claude to actually know our business when it does SEO work for us. Set up an Obsidian vault for this and tell me how to dump everything in.
evals.expected_output: Scaffolds the full vault tree (00-INDEX as entry point, company/, market/, content/, people/, seo/ with action-log.md in the documented format, sources/), drafts the company and market notes with TODO markers where facts are missing, and delivers a batched dump plan (10-20 documents per batch, prioritized: identity and product docs first, then call transcripts for customer language, then past SEO work). Explains the routing rule (a dump is done when its facts are findable from the index, not when the file is converted), the one-fact-one-note rule, the single-source-of-truth rule for numbers, and the no-secrets rule.

evals.prompt: I already have an Obsidian vault at ~/Documents/acme-vault with notes about our product and customers. Now write me a blog post about industrial label printers. Why do you keep asking me questions about our company?
evals.expected_output: Applies the read-first protocol: reads the entry point then the relevant notes (identity, product, customers, keywords map, action log) before writing anything, grounds the article brief in the vault's facts and customer language instead of asking the user, checks the action log and published.md to avoid duplicating an existing article, then hands the actual writing to the seo-content-blog skill with the vault context attached, and ends by appending a dated entry to seo/action-log.md.

evals.prompt: ok we just finished fixing the titles and meta descriptions on 12 collection pages and added the schema. anything else before I close this?
evals.expected_output: Applies the write-back protocol: appends one dated entry to seo/action-log.md in the exact documented format (skill used, action, pages touched, expected effect, check-on date), quotes the entry back to the user, updates content/published.md or the relevant notes if pages changed, and suggests the check-back date for verifying impact. Refuses to end the session without logging.

evals.prompt: I'm a solo founder. My business and my personal life are completely mixed (clients who are friends, expenses that are half personal). I want one Obsidian vault for everything but I don't want it to become a mess. How should I structure it so an AI can always find things fast?
evals.expected_output: Recommends the layered architecture from references/vault-architecture.md: two entry points (00-INDEX for business, a personal index) that link to each other, one domain hub per area, MOCs only for large bases, atomic notes underneath, everything reachable from the top in one or two hops. Explains the token-economy reason (the agent reads the entry point in full, then follows links, never a full-text search) and the linking rules (no orphans, bidirectional links, one fact one note, single source of truth for numbers). Notes that a person who is both client and friend gets one note linked from both sides.

evals.prompt: Most of our real client history is in WhatsApp: hundreds of conversations, prices we quoted, objections, promises. How do I get that into the vault so Claude knows it, without it being a mess?
evals.expected_output: Gives the WhatsApp workflow from references/import-workflows.md: install WhatsApp Desktop so chats are readable locally, export the conversations that carry business (per-chat text export, without media), write one note per contact with frontmatter and extracted signal (dated summary plus verbatim quotes that carry objections, pricing, commitments) rather than pasting raw lines, then merge each into that person's existing CRM note so there is one note per human. Recommends multi-agent fan-out for the large backlog (one sub-agent per slice of contacts, central reconciliation) and running scripts/person_matches.py afterward to catch duplicates. Flags that secrets in chats never enter the vault.

evals.prompt: My vault has grown to a couple thousand notes over a year and it feels broken: dead links, notes I can't find from the index, the same client showing up twice. Can you check it and fix it?
evals.expected_output: Runs the link audit from references/link-audit.md: scripts/link_graph.py to list broken links, orphans, notes unreachable from the entry point and duplicate basenames, and scripts/person_matches.py to find the same person across folders. Then works the fix playbook in order (repair or remove broken links, link orphans into their hub, merge duplicate people into one canonical note and update inbound links, path-qualify ambiguous links, rename files with wikilink-hostile characters), re-runs the audit to confirm zero broken/orphan/unreachable, and logs the audit as an action-log entry with counts before and after.
